\subsection*{Randomized --- ZPPEquiv: Results}

\begin{definition}[Bounded-error exponential-time decision]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInExpTime}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInExpTime}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.randProb, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.ExpTimeLe, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of finite Boolean strings, and let $T$ be a time bound. On every input $x$,
the expected running time of $N$ is at most $T(|x|)$. Moreover, for every rational
$\varepsilon>0$, there is a natural number $t$ such that, on a uniformly random
choice string of length $t$, the probability that $N$ halts with output equal to the
indicator of $x\in L$ is at least $2/3-\varepsilon$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Exponential-time probabilistic languages]
\lean{Randomized.BPP_ExpPTM}
\label{Randomized.BPP_ExpPTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInExpTime}
The class consists of the languages $L$ of finite Boolean strings for which there exist
natural numbers $e,c$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over Booleans
such that $N$ satisfies the bounded-error exponential-time decision condition for $L$
with time bound $n\mapsto c(n^e+1)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Efficient verifier for halting runs]
\lean{Randomized.exists_eff_haltRun}
\label{Randomized.exists_eff_haltRun}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.append, Complexity.compl_mem_P, Complexity.exists_choiceVerifier_mem_P, Complexity.inter_mem_P, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairSndD, Complexity.preimage_mem_P, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.flipOutput, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_flipOutput, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine and let $A,e$ be natural numbers.
There is an efficient verifier $M$ with values in
$\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true},\mathrm{undefined}\}$ such that, for every pair of bit
strings $x,r$ with $|r|=A(|x|+1)^e$ and every bit $b$, $M(x,r)=b$ if and only if the run
of $N$ on input $x$ under choices $r$ halts with output exactly the one-bit word $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time zero-error verifier characterization]
\lean{Randomized.inZPP_of_mem_ZPP_PTM}
\label{Randomized.inZPP_of_mem_ZPP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.InZPP, Randomized.ZPP_PTM, Randomized.exists_eff_haltRun, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_mono, Randomized.randProb_not, Turing.FinNDTM.ExpTimeLe.one_le, Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime.truncate, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.choiceBudget_le}
\difficulty{5}
Let $L$ be a language of bit strings. If $L$ belongs to the class defined as the union,
over natural numbers $c$, of languages decidable by a finite nondeterministic Turing
machine with expected running-time bound $n^c+1$ in the stated polynomial-time model,
then $L$ has an efficient polynomial-witness verifier that never gives an incorrect
answer and gives no answer with probability at most $1/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Abort-machine characterization of zero-error computation]
\lean{Randomized.inZPP_of_mem_ZPPAbort_PTM}
\label{Randomized.inZPP_of_mem_ZPPAbort_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.InZPP, Randomized.ZPPAbort_PTM, Randomized.exists_eff_haltRun, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_mono, Randomized.randProb_not, Randomized.randProb_take, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.FinNDTM.runWith_eq_runWith_take, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin.mono, Turing.choiceBudget_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let $L$ be a language of bit strings. If there are a natural number $c$ and a finite
nondeterministic Turing machine whose running time on inputs of length $n$ is bounded by
$a(n^c+1)$ for some natural number $a$, such that every length-matched choice string
makes the machine halt, its output is never the one-bit indicator of membership in $L$,
and that output equals the indicator with probability at least $1/2$ under uniformly
random choices, then $L$ has an efficient polynomial-witness verifier with no incorrect
answers and probability at most $1/2$ of giving no answer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected-time randomized decision implies polynomial-time verification]
\lean{Randomized.inBPP_of_mem_BPP_ExpPTM}
\label{Randomized.inBPP_of_mem_BPP_ExpPTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.exists_choiceVerifier_mem_P, Randomized.BPP_ExpPTM, Randomized.InBPP, Randomized.InBPPAt.inBPP_of_5_8, Randomized.eff_append_mem, Randomized.indicator_eq_true_iff, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.polyTimeModel_closedUnderMajority, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_mono, Turing.FinNDTM.haltProb_le_truncate, Turing.FinNDTM.haltProb_mono, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.choiceBudget_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let $L$ be a language of bit strings. If a finite nondeterministic Turing machine
decides membership in $L$ with acceptance probability at least $2/3-\varepsilon$ for
every positive rational $\varepsilon$, and for every input its sum of probabilities of
not having halted by each time up to any finite cutoff is bounded by a polynomial in the
input length, then there is a polynomial-time randomized verifier whose acceptance
probability is at least $2/3$ on members of $L$ and whose rejection probability is at
least $2/3$ on nonmembers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial randomized time and expected time]
\lean{Randomized.BPP_PTM_subset_BPP_ExpPTM}

\leanok

\begin{theorem}[Expected-time and polynomial-time BPP coincide]
\lean{Randomized.BPP_ExpPTM_eq_BPP_PTM}
\label{Randomized.BPP_ExpPTM_eq_BPP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPP_ExpPTM, Randomized.BPP_PTM, Randomized.BPP_PTM_subset_BPP_ExpPTM, Randomized.inBPP_of_mem_BPP_ExpPTM, Randomized.mem_BPP_PTM_iff}
\difficulty{1}
The class of languages decidable by a finite-state randomized Turing machine whose
expected running time is polynomial in the input length and whose probability of
producing the correct answer can be made at least $2/3-\varepsilon$ for every
$\varepsilon>0$ equals the class decidable in polynomial worst-case time with
probability at least $2/3$ of producing the correct answer.
\end{theorem}
